events.title: First Spacewalk by Alexei Leonov
events.description: Soviet cosmonaut Alexei Leonov exited the Voskhod 2 spacecraft and floated in open space for about 12 minutes, tethered to the capsule. He had difficulty re-entering because his suit had ballooned in the vacuum, and he had to bleed off some air to get back inside.
events.significance: This was the first extravehicular activity in history, proving humans could survive and work outside a spacecraft, a capability essential for later space stations and lunar missions.

events.title: Execution of Jacques de Molay
events.description: The last Grand Master of the Knights Templar, Jacques de Molay, was burned at the stake in Paris on the orders of King Philip IV of France, after the order had been accused of heresy and other crimes.
events.significance: His death marked the effective end of the powerful Templar order and showed the growing power of the French monarchy over the church and wealthy institutions. It also fueled centuries of legend and conspiracy theories.

events.title: Mahatma Gandhi Sentenced to Six Years in Prison
events.description: Mohandas K. Gandhi was convicted of sedition by British colonial authorities in India for articles he wrote in his journal Young India that criticized British rule. He was sentenced to six years in prison, though he was released early in 1924 for medical reasons.
events.significance: The trial became a landmark in the Indian independence movement, and Gandhi's dignified statement in court strengthened the moral force of his nonviolent civil disobedience campaign.

events.title: Mexico Nationalizes Its Oil Industry
events.description: President Lázaro Cárdenas announced the expropriation of foreign-owned oil companies operating in Mexico, mostly British and American, after the companies refused to comply with a Supreme Court ruling on labor disputes and wages.
events.significance: The nationalization led to the creation of Pemex in 1938 and became a symbol of Mexican economic sovereignty. March 18 is still commemorated in Mexico as a national day.

events.title: Russia Annexes Crimea
events.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a treaty incorporating Crimea and the city of Sevastopol into the Russian Federation, following a disputed referendum held days earlier. Ukraine and most of the international community rejected the move as illegal.
events.significance: The annexation was the first forcible change of European borders since World War II, triggered international sanctions on Russia, and set the stage for the war in eastern Ukraine and the 2022 full-scale invasion.
